static_traits.name: Amanda
static_traits.social_status: Weak social support; not many friends, and hard to open up to existing friends
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; never received psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly with good logic, can describe events and feelings; fairly cooperative; tone carries significant anxiety and self-denial

basic_info.main_problem: After being unable to answer a visitor's question about an exhibit at the museum, felt incompetent and afraid of losing the job, even believing I will never find another job.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizing own reactions and thinking patterns may affect mental health and work stability, hoping to identify the problems and the beliefs behind them, challenge catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking, and practice specific coping strategies to reduce anxiety and improve work performance.

core_beliefs: As long as I make a mistake at work, it proves I am a failure
I am not competent enough for this job
I should know the exhibits inside out; otherwise I do not deserve to be competent

special_situations.event: At the museum, being questioned by a visitor about a piece and unable to answer on the spot
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot immediately answer any question about the exhibits, it means I am incompetent and may be fired
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Seeks reassurance from colleagues and tries hard to avoid making mistakes again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will lose my job, and never find a new job

special_situations.event: Feeling embarrassed in front of colleagues for not being able to answer
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I embarrass myself in front of colleagues, everyone will think I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive self-monitoring at work, reducing exposure to situations where questioning may occur
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I am not good enough and will look down on me

special_situations.event: Whenever a small mistake happens at work or I am not familiar with an exhibit
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make one mistake, it means I am fundamentally not suited to this job
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcing myself to be perfect, over-analyzing every step to avoid mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a failure / not suited to this job

special_situations.event: When reviewing the day's work, only focusing on the one question I could not answer
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not answer all questions well, it does not count as doing the job well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores completed work and correct answers, continuously ruminates on failure episodes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This shows I am no good; my performance is terrible

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as competent and to maintain job stability
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being denied, being looked down on by colleagues, being fired
defense_goal: Maintains high standards and perfection to avoid criticism
Reduce anxiety by seeking reassurance from others
Avoid exposing inadequacy to keep a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: An employee not competent enough, prone to embarrassment

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking about or discussing how others (colleagues, visitors) view one's own mistakes
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will look down on me, thinking I am not good enough (transference: projecting inner self-denial onto outside evaluation)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Ask for evidence and counterexamples in a gentle, specific way; keep an empathy tone; invite specific events rather than inferences; promptly label 'this is a thought, not a fact'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor offers a reasonable interpretation (e.g., being asked about an unfamiliar piece, having one's train of thought interrupted on the spot) and tries to reduce guilt and shame
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Even if the reasons are reasonable, I should still be perfect; otherwise I do not deserve to be competent (absorbing external standards undigested)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Acknowledge the intent behind the high standards (wanting to do the job well), while gently distinguishing 'ideal standards' from 'realistic feasibility'; use specific situations to reconstruct the standard of 'good enough'; steady tone, slow pace, use examples.

manifestations: Not many friends; hard to open up to existing friends about anxiety
Social support system not strong; work stress mostly digested alone
outcomes: More prone to catastrophizing and excessive self-blame at work
More dependent on external reassurance and lacking inner self-acceptance

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Repeatedly emphasize 'I should know the exhibits inside out, cannot make mistakes'
Treats perfectionist standards as the only acceptable rule

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on.
manifestations: Over-analyzes every step at work, excessive self-reproach
Highly nervous in front of colleagues, worries about others' evaluations, leading to abnormal performance

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Believe colleagues will look down on oneself, visitors will think oneself not good enough
From this, strong shame and fear arise, thus intensifying avoidance

positive_force: Has a professional background in art history and museum work experience
Able to propose concrete coping plans (such as replying after verifying, or referring to a more familiar colleague)
Willing to try breaking down problems and practicing more feasible responses
negative_force: Catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, mind reading and mental filtering
Weak social support, hard to express anxiety to friends
Frequently seeks external reassurance and lacks internal self-acceptance
Anxiety leads to sleep disturbed and decline in work performance

target_behavior.behavior: Frequently seeks reassurance from colleagues at work (reassurance seeking)
antecedent: Being questioned by visitors about unfamiliar pieces
Small mistakes in front of colleagues or worrying about others' evaluations
Recalling the day's mistakes and ruminating
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive biases like catastrophizing and mind reading trigger fear of being fired and looked down on; hoping others' reassurance will briefly relieve anxiety
target_behavior.function: Gain comfort and a sense of safety; reduce anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Dependence on external comfort grows, internal self-acceptance weakens; anxiety does not substantially decline yet, further affecting work performance and sleep

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive self-monitoring and avoiding situations where mistakes may occur (perfectionism-driven caution and avoidance)
antecedent: Needing to explain exhibits in front of colleagues or visitors
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by introjected perfection standards and black-and-white thinking, viewing one mistake as a total failure; trying to prevent exposing inadequacy again through avoidance
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential criticism and shame, maintaining a surface sense of safety
target_behavior.consequence: Learning and practice opportunities decrease; actual sense of competence does not improve; anxiety is maintained or even worsened
